title: Proxima Centauri

description:
Episode 10 of a daily journey through the universe. ⭐
We leave the solar system for Proxima Centauri: 40 trillion km away, light that left it more than four years ago, a 70,000-year trip at Voyager's speed, and a planet in the habitable zone.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 11: Next stop, a black hole. And what would happen if you fell in.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

#space #proximacentauri #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode ten. Next stop... our nearest star.
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our Sun. But it's still about forty trillion kilometers away.
segments.headline: 40 trillion km away

segments.text: That's four point two light-years. The light you see from it tonight left more than four years ago.

visual.label: light-years away
visual.sub: You see it as it was 4 years ago

segments.text: Even at Voyager's speed, the trip would take more than seventy thousand years.
It's a small red dwarf, cooler and dimmer than our Sun, and it blasts out powerful flares.
segments.headline: A small red dwarf

segments.text: And it has a planet, Proxima b, a little more massive than Earth, in the zone where liquid water could exist.
segments.headline: A planet in the habitable zone

segments.text: Tomorrow, we visit the most extreme objects in the universe. Next stop: a black hole, and what would happen if you fell in. Follow, so you don't miss episode eleven.
